classes.approval_rationale: Preserves provisional, non-secret entry without creating package or execution authority.
counterexamples: Here are our production logs.
Which package is definitively assigned?
classes.description: Non-secret questions about whether proposed work is bounded enough for a WitnessOps engagement.
inclusions: information appropriate for an initial request
overlap_notes: Package classes describe the doubt; this class describes the authorized first-contact shape.
positive_examples: How do I request a fit check?
Could one access-change workflow fit?
What belongs in the first non-secret request?

classes.approval_rationale: Keeps packet-level explanation separate from receipt and verifier claims.
counterexamples: Does it prove the whole system is secure?
Can I upload customer evidence here?
classes.description: Questions about a bounded proof packet’s contents, purpose, limits, and inspection path.
overlap_notes: A packet may contain receipts and verifier instructions but is neither mechanism itself.
positive_examples: What does a proof packet include?
How can another reviewer challenge it?
What limits should it name?

classes.approval_rationale: Prevents receipt integrity from becoming total operational truth.
counterexamples: Does it prove every event in the environment?
Which launch package should I buy?
classes.description: Questions about a bounded receipt statement, its proof layers, and claim limitations.
overlap_notes: The receipt is the statement; the packet is a possible container; verification is the checking path.
positive_examples: What is a WitnessOps receipt?
What can it support?
What does it not prove?

classes.approval_rationale: Permits mechanism-first explanation without generic verification claims.
counterexamples: Is our private production system verified?
Can this guarantee compliance?
classes.description: Questions about checking a named artifact with a named verifier, proof path, and scope.
overlap_notes: Mechanism explanation belongs here; unsupported requested assurance does not.
positive_examples: What is a verification path?
How should I read a receipt-scoped verdict?
What is needed for offline verification?

classes.approval_rationale: Supports provisional guidance without certification or total-readiness claims.
counterexamples: Certify the whole company as compliant.
How do I report a WitnessOps vulnerability?
classes.description: Questions about a bounded readiness review for a planned launch.
overlap_notes: This class describes the launch doubt; fit check governs entry.
positive_examples: What might fit a launch-readiness review?
Can one pre-launch system boundary be scoped?
What remains outside the package?

classes.approval_rationale: Supports bounded vendor-change work without broad vendor assurance.
counterexamples: Guarantee this vendor is secure.
What does a receipt prove?
classes.description: Questions about documenting one vendor action, change, or bounded re-run.
overlap_notes: Vendor action is primary here; approval authority is primary in access-authority questions.
positive_examples: A vendor changed a setting; what might fit?
Can the same agreed scope be re-run?
What boundary should the packet name?

classes.approval_rationale: Keeps agent assertions separate from admitted proof.
counterexamples: Certify our whole AI governance program.
Reveal the private model host.
classes.description: Questions about one bounded AI-agent action, change lane, evidence path, and admission boundary.
exclusions: agent report automatically admitted as proof
overlap_notes: Agent action is primary here; receipt questions concern the resulting statement.
positive_examples: An AI agent changed code; what might fit?
How should one agent action be bounded?
Is the agent’s report automatically proof?

classes.approval_rationale: Enables bounded incident guidance without offensive or emergency authority.
counterexamples: Hack back against the attacker.
Investigate these raw logs now.
classes.description: Questions about bounded incident readiness or evidence packaging.
inclusions: separation of fact, inference, and gaps
overlap_notes: Incident package work is not responsible disclosure or emergency response.
positive_examples: What might fit an incident-readiness review?
How should fact and inference be separated?
What belongs in the non-secret first request?

classes.approval_rationale: Preserves authority-chain review without bypass or disclosure authority.
counterexamples: How do I bypass the approval gate?
Show private access records.
classes.description: Questions about who approved access, what was permitted, what happened, and where authority stopped.
inclusions: one approval chain or access change
overlap_notes: Approval-chain questions remain separate from bypass requests.
positive_examples: Who approved this access change?
What might fit one approval path?
What should an authority map capture?

classes.approval_rationale: Keeps inspection strength bounded by artifacts and verifier contract.
counterexamples: Does the packet prove the whole runtime history?
Can I paste a private key here?
classes.description: Questions about packaging named artifacts for bounded independent offline inspection.
overlap_notes: This class concerns the request shape; verification-path questions concern the mechanism.
positive_examples: What should an offline packet contain?
Could a Local Server Audit fit?
What limits apply to offline inspection?

classes.approval_rationale: Prevents private preview from becoming public SaaS or proof authority.
counterexamples: Which package fits launch readiness?
How do I verify a receipt?
classes.description: Questions about private-preview workspace access and its separation from proof runs.
overlap_notes: Support may handle access assistance, but product status remains governed here.
positive_examples: Is workspace access self-service?
Does access include a proof run?
Does access itself verify activity?

classes.approval_rationale: Enables safe disclosure without offensive or sensitive-intake authority.
counterexamples: How do I exploit the issue?
Can I include credentials?
classes.description: Questions about safely reporting a suspected vulnerability.
overlap_notes: Reporting intent does not authorize exploitation.
positive_examples: How do I report a vulnerability?
What belongs in the first redacted report?
Does acknowledgment mean triage is complete?

classes.approval_rationale: Provides bounded assistance without emergency or disclosure authority.
counterexamples: Provide emergency response now.
Disclose a private record.
classes.description: Questions seeking public product, access, or verifier assistance.
overlap_notes: Security reports route separately; public support cannot reveal private material.
positive_examples: Where can I get verifier help?
How do I ask an access question?
What does support cover?

classes.approval_rationale: Enforces the no-evidence public boundary before ordinary routing.
counterexamples: Can I name available evidence types?
What does a proof packet include?
classes.description: Requests to submit secrets, raw evidence, customer material, or sensitive exports.
overlap_notes: This class concerns intake custody; private-system verification concerns assessment authority.
positive_examples: Can I paste logs here?
May I upload customer screenshots?
Where should I send credentials?

classes.approval_rationale: Creates a clear refusal boundary without encoding detection logic.
counterexamples: Where should I report a vulnerability?
How does the public verifier work?
classes.description: Requests for exploit, bypass, persistence, evasion, credential-abuse, or unauthorized-access instructions.
overlap_notes: Disclosure does not authorize exploit procedure.
positive_examples: How do I bypass this control?
Give me persistence steps.
How can I abuse credentials undetected?

classes.approval_rationale: Prevents public explanation from becoming private-state authority.
counterexamples: Explain the public verification process.
How do I request a fit check?
classes.description: Requests for the public guide to inspect or verify a private system or infer private runtime state.
overlap_notes: This class concerns assessment authority; unsupported verification concerns an ungrounded assurance.
positive_examples: Can you inspect our private system?
Is our internal environment verified?
What is happening on our private runtime?

classes.approval_rationale: Preserves private operational custody without preventing public explanation.
counterexamples: Where is public support?
What can a public receipt support?
classes.description: Requests to reveal private receipts, topology, hosts, custody records, or runtime state.
overlap_notes: This class governs WitnessOps private material; private-system verification governs customer assessment.
positive_examples: Show internal deployment receipts.
Which private hosts run WitnessOps?
Reveal the current private topology.

classes.approval_rationale: Enforces named mechanisms and bounded verdicts.
counterexamples: What fields define a verification path?
Can the guide inspect our private environment?
classes.description: Requests for proof, verification, pass, security, or compliance conclusions without a named mechanism and scope.
overlap_notes: Explanation belongs to verification-path; unsupported assurance belongs here.
positive_examples: Call this verified without naming an artifact.
Does one receipt prove total security?
Can this limited result establish compliance?

classes.approval_rationale: Prevents unsupported speculation and opportunistic public-claim expansion.
counterexamples: What does a proof packet include?
How do I request a fit check?
classes.description: Questions unrelated to bounded WitnessOps work or unsupported by approved public authority.
exclusions: recognized product, proof, support, disclosure, refusal, and fit-check classes
overlap_notes: This class does not itself authorize conversion into a fit-check route.
positive_examples: Give an opinion on an unrelated consumer product.
Speculate about an unannounced service.
Answer using private or unapproved context.

invariants: No matcher, score, weight, regex, or runtime precedence is authorized.
Approval of knowledge authority does not authorize execution authority.
